To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CD of myelin, synaptosomal and synaptic vesicle membranes from rat brain differ significantly, that the CD of these membranes is affected by temperature, pH and electrolytes, and that these effects are specific in nature.
the CD spectra of three different membrane preparations from rat cerebral cortex were different, and that these differences were not accounted for by turbidity effects.
1) The CD of membrane preparations is affected by the physical and chemical conditions of the preparation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a method for the study of membrane structure by circular dichroism.
the development of a new approach to the analysis of membrane structure and function.
the elucidation of the three‐dimensional conformation of membrane proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CD of membrane proteins is sensitive to a wide range of physical and chemical factors, including temperature, pH, ionic strength, and the presence of other membrane components.
membrane CD spectra are sensitive to the environment of membranes.
the CD of membrane preparations is not a simple function of the CD of the constituent protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CD spectra of membrane fractions can be used to detect differences in the structure of the proteins of different membrane fractions.

the CD of nerve membrane preparations is not a simple, invariant function of the membrane protein structure. 1 The effects of temperature, pH and electrolytes on the circular dichroism of nerve membrane fractions were investigated.

the CD of membrane fractions is sensitive to changes in pH, temperature, electrolytes, and to other factors such as the presence of detergents, and that these effects may be due to alterations in the secondary structure of the protein components of the membranes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

CD spectra can reveal differences in the three‐dimensional organization of proteins in different membranes, but these differences are likely to be obscured by turbidity effects and by the perturbation of the membrane by the environment in which it is placed.

CD can be a valuable technique for studying the structure of nerve membrane preparations, and can be applied in conjunction with other techniques to yield useful information about the structure and function of these complex biological membranes.
the CD spectra of membrane preparations may be used to detect differences in the structure of membrane proteins.
